section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as an Instruction
section_1.content: Define a vector as an arrow in 2D space. Introduce the concept of 'scaling' and 'adding' vectors as movement instructions on a grid.
section_1.example: A robot arm moving 2 units right (vector i) and 3 units up (vector j) to reach a coordinate (2,3).

section_2.title: Linear Combinations and Span
section_2.content: Explain that a linear combination is the result of scaling and adding vectors. The 'Span' is the set of all reachable points in space using these vectors.
section_2.example: Visualizing two vectors as 'drawing tools'; if they point in different directions, their span covers the entire 2D plane (like painting a wall).

section_3.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
section_3.content: Introduce linear dependence: if one vector lies on the span of the others, it provides no new information. Visually, this is a vector that lies on the same line as another.
section_3.example: Two squirrels running in the same direction; the second squirrel is redundant because it doesn't help the group reach any new territory.

section_4.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
section_4.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that is both linearly independent and spans the entire space. It is the 'minimal set' of instructions needed to describe every point in the space.
section_4.example: Using standard basis vectors (1,0) and (0,1) as a GPS coordinate system; you need exactly these two to uniquely identify any location on a map.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Summary
section_5.content: Connect the concepts: Linear combinations form the span. If vectors are independent, they form a basis. If dependent, they contain redundant information.
section_5.example: A summary animation showing a 2D plane shrinking to a line (dependence) and expanding back to a plane when a new, independent vector is added.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shifted right to avoid occlusion with lecture
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Spans represent all possible reaches.",
            "Basis defines a minimal framework.",
            "Independence prevents redundant information.",
            "Redundancy collapses our total span.",
            "Summary: Basis describes space efficiently."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup for vectors
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)
        
        v1 = Vector([2, 1], color=YELLOW)
        v2 = Vector([-1, 2], color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1, 2 & 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), 
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
